newsitem.title: USA: US T-bond yield touches 6.50 pct on benign data.
newsitem.headline: US T-bond yield touches 6.50 pct on benign data.

text.p: The U.S. Treasury bond climbed to session highs at mid-morning, its yield touching 6.50 percent, a seven-month low.

The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose as much as 19/32 as its yield slipped to 6.50 percent on benign economic data that included a smaller than expected 0.1 percent increase in the June Consumer Price Index (CPI) and a moderate 0.3 percent rise in June industrial production, analysts said.
Economists said the Federal Reserve's production and capacity utilization statistics reflected moderate economic growth that was putting no pressure on capacity.
That combination boded well for continued subdued inflation, they said.
The 6.50 percent bond yield was the lowest for the benchmark security since the close on December 10 of 1996.

"We had friendly data this morning," said Josh Stiles, senior bond strategist at I.D.E.A. "The rise is all accounted for by the CPI being lower than expected and industrial production showing no rise in the capacity rate. That's a good combination reflecting on-going, good fundamentals."
(( E. Freilich, North American Treasury Desk 212-859-1679))
